transcript: Okay, this is the basement. I'd want the kitchen over here by the stairs, my mom would sleep in sleep in this room by the window
headline: Yes, if you fix 2 things.
wants: You want a kitchen by the stairs and a bedroom by the window for your mom.
summary: The basement is open and unfinished with exposed joists, ducts and mechanicals. Window, separation and exit checks need work or measurements for a Waterloo second unit.

findings.title: Up to four homes on the lot
findings.plain: Waterloo allows additional residential units in detached, freehold semi-detached and townhouse buildings, up to 3 ARUs (4 homes in total) and at most one coach house per lot.
findings.why: The video does not show how many homes are on the lot or the house type.
findings.question: How many separate homes with kitchens and bathrooms are on the lot now, and is the house detached, semi-detached or a townhouse?

source.title: City of Waterloo Zoning By-law 2018-050 (consolidated 23 March 2026)
source.section: s. 3.A.1B.1 and 3.A.1B.2(d); Table 7A (R1) 'Number of DWELLING UNITS per LOT (maximum) 4'

findings.title: Must be on City water and sewer
findings.plain: An ARU must be connected to municipal sanitary sewer and municipal water.
findings.why: The video does not show the water and sewer connections.
findings.question: Is the house on City water and City sewer, not well or septic?

source.title: City of Waterloo Zoning By-law 2018-050 (consolidated 23 March 2026)

findings.title: Ceiling height in the suite: 1.95 m
findings.plain: Ceilings in the new suite must be at least 1.95 m high, and the areas that meet the height must connect to each room's entrance.
findings.why: The finished ceiling height cannot be told from the unfinished video.
findings.question: What is the lowest floor to ceiling height after finishes?

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

findings.title: Clearance under beams and ducts: 1.85 m
findings.plain: Under beams and ductwork inside the suite, the clear height must be at least 1.85 m.
findings.why: Beams and ducts are visible overhead and their clearance is unknown.
findings.question: What is the lowest clearance under any beam or duct after finishes?

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

findings.title: Bedroom escape window: 0.35 m² opening
findings.plain: Every floor level with a bedroom needs at least one outside window that opens from inside without tools, stays open by itself and gives an unobstructed opening of at least 0.35 m², unless that level has a door straight to the outside.
findings.why: The bedroom window looks small and high and likely gives too little escape opening.

fix.description: Cut and enlarge the foundation opening and install an egress-size window with a code-compliant window well.

costSource.title: Basement Renovation Cost Guide: Kitchener-Waterloo & Cambridge 2026

fix.costNote: Estimate, not a quote. Waterloo Region contractor guide. HomeStars (Canada) gives $3,500-$8,000 for a new opening with window and well; a Toronto source gives $7,500-$17,000. See costs[].

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

findings.title: Bedroom escape window: no side under 380 mm
findings.plain: The escape window's clear opening must be at least 380 mm in every direction; for sliders, measure only the part that opens.
findings.why: The bedroom window looks narrow and likely has a side under 380 mm.

fix.description: Same as egress_window_bedroom_area (larger window, possibly a casement).

costSource.title: Basement Renovation Cost Guide: Kitchener-Waterloo & Cambridge 2026

fix.costNote: Estimate, not a quote; shared with the window enlargement fix.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

findings.title: Window well: 550 mm clear in front
findings.plain: If the escape window opens into a window well, keep at least 550 mm clear in front of it (beyond any outward-opening sash), and any well cover must open from inside without keys or tools.
findings.why: It is not clear if the bedroom window opens into a well.
findings.question: Does the window open into a well and how far to the well wall?

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

findings.title: Fire/smoke separation between the two homes
findings.plain: Separate the suite from the rest of the house with a 45-minute fire separation, or with a continuous smoke-tight barrier of 15.9 mm (5/8 in.) Type X drywall on both sides of dividing walls and under the floor/ceiling framing. The rating can be waived if the house is sprinklered.
findings.why: The ceiling joists are open with no fire-rated drywall seen.

fix.description: Install 5/8 in. Type X drywall on the suite ceiling and on both sides of dividing walls, keep it continuous and seal joints and penetrations; add self-closing doors where the separation has openings.

costSource.title: Cost to Make a Basement Legal in Toronto

fix.costNote: Estimate, not a quote (Toronto, 2026, 'fire separation' line). Ceiling drywall installed and finished is $4.00-$6.50/sq ft before the Type X upgrade (see costs[]).

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

findings.title: Furnace room separation
findings.plain: If the furnace or water heater serves both units, put it in a service room lined with 15.9 mm (5/8 in.) Type X drywall on both sides of its walls and on the underside of the ceiling framing; otherwise fuel-fired appliances need a 1-hour fire separation.
findings.why: The furnace and water heater sit open to the space with no separate room.

fix.description: Enclose the furnace/water heater in its own room and line its walls (both sides) and ceiling with 5/8 in. Type X drywall.
fix.costNote: No separate price found; usually part of the fire separation work.

check.appliesWhen: a fuel-fired appliance serves both dwelling units

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

findings.title: Interconnected smoke alarms in both homes
findings.plain: Put smoke alarms on every storey, in every bedroom and outside sleeping areas of each unit, and in shared exits and common areas, then interconnect them (hard-wired or wireless) so any one alarm sounds all alarms in both homes.
findings.why: No smoke alarms or interconnection can be seen in the video.
findings.question: Is there a smoke alarm on every level and in each bedroom, and do they all sound together?

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

findings.title: Interconnected carbon monoxide alarms
findings.plain: If the house has a fuel-burning appliance (such as a gas furnace or water heater) or an attached garage, put CO alarms next to the sleeping rooms in each unit and in the service room, interconnected so one alarm sounds all CO alarms in the house.
findings.why: A furnace and water heater are visible and CO alarm setup is unknown.
findings.question: Is the furnace or water heater gas, oil or propane, and are CO alarms near bedrooms that sound together?

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B
source.section: 9.32.3.9C.(1) (interconnection within a house with a secondary suite)

findings.title: A safe way out of the suite
findings.plain: Best: the suite has its own door to the outside. A shared exit is allowed if it is separated by a 30-minute fire separation, does not pass through the other home or a service room, and both homes have interconnected smoke alarms. Leaving through the other home is only allowed with an extra escape window and interconnected alarms, or if the house is sprinklered.
findings.why: Stairs and a door at the top are visible but the outside path is unclear.
findings.question: How would someone leave the basement home in a fire: its own outside door, a shared hall, or through the upstairs home?

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division B Part 11

findings.title: No shared air between the homes
findings.plain: Each home's air ducts may not be directly connected to the other home, and air from one suite may not be recirculated to the other. In a house 5+ years old, one existing forced-air system may serve both if each unit has smoke alarms and a duct smoke detector shuts off the furnace's fuel and power when it detects smoke.
findings.why: Ducts and a furnace are visible and sharing between homes is unclear.
findings.question: Does one furnace heat both floors, and are there return grilles in the basement?

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

findings.title: Separate ESA electrical permit and inspection
findings.plain: Electrical work for the suite needs its own Electrical Safety Authority (ESA) permit and inspection, separate from the City building permit; Ontario recommends a licensed electrical contractor.
findings.why: The video does not show permits or electrical plans.
findings.question: Will a licensed contractor take out a separate ESA permit for the suite?

source.title: Add a second unit to your house (Government of Ontario, updated 2023-01-30)

findings.title: Kitchen, bathroom, hot water and its own water shut-off
findings.plain: The suite needs a kitchen sink, a bathroom sink, a toilet and a tub or shower with hot water, access to laundry (it can be shared), a floor drain in its basement, and its own water shut-off valve where the supply enters the unit.
findings.why: No kitchen, bathroom or shut-off can be seen in the video.
findings.question: Is there a basement bathroom or capped pipes in the floor, and where does water enter?

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium (MMAH), Division B

grants.name: City of Waterloo ARU Grant, Interior ARU stream
grants.amount: Up to 50% of eligible project costs, maximum $20,000 for an interior unit such as a basement apartment (the Detached ARU stream is up to $30,000).
grants.fitNote: Family members (parent, grandparent, sibling, child, grandchild, aunt/uncle, cousin) can be the tenant if they pay rent at or under the cap and their household income is under the limit; the owner's spouse or a dependent cannot. A rental only fits at the affordable rent for 5 years.
grants.nextStep: Apply before construction starts at https://forms.waterloo.ca/Grants/Apply-for-an-additional-residential-unit-grant ; email ARU@waterloo.ca with questions.

source.title: Apply for the ARU Grant (City of Waterloo)
source.section: Check if you can apply; Review rent and tenant rules; 2026 maximum affordable rent and income

grants.name: Region of Waterloo Ontario Renovates - Secondary Suites (forgivable loan)
grants.amount: Up to $25,000 per property, interest-free, forgiven evenly over 15 years (includes up to $5,000 for accessibility work that is a grant).
grants.fitNote: The Region pitches it for an 'affordable in-law suite', but every occupant is treated as a tenant who must pass income verification and pay rent at or under the cap. Requires the owner to live in the house for 15 years.
grants.nextStep: Confirm zoning with the City, then send the application to OntarioRenovates@regionofwaterloo.ca before any work starts.

source.title: Funding for Secondary Suites (Region of Waterloo)
source.section: Who is eligible; How to apply

grants.name: Multigenerational Home Renovation Tax Credit (MHRTC), line 45355
grants.amount: For 2025: 14.5% of up to $50,000 of qualifying costs per qualifying renovation (maximum $7,250). For renovations completed in 2026 the rate is expected to be 14% (maximum $7,000); not yet confirmed on the CRA page.
grants.fitNote: Only for a suite that lets a senior (65+) or an adult eligible for the disability tax credit live with a qualifying relative. Not for a rental to an unrelated tenant.
grants.nextStep: Keep all receipts and the permit; claim on line 45355 of the tax return for the year the renovation is completed.

source.title: Line 45355 - Multigenerational home renovation tax credit (CRA)

grants.name: Development charge exemption for a second or third unit in an existing house
grants.amount: City of Waterloo and Region of Waterloo development charges are not charged for a 2nd or 3rd unit in an existing detached, semi-detached or row house (the City charges DCs only on a 4th unit).
grants.nextStep: Nothing to apply for; confirm at permit stage whether any education development charge is billed.

source.title: Development Charges Act, 1997, S.O. 1997, c. 27

grants.name: CMHC-insured refinance for building a secondary suite
grants.amount: Refinance up to 90% of the as-improved home value (value under $2,000,000), amortization up to 30 years; money must go to building the suite.
grants.fitNote: Financing, not free money: it lets you borrow against the finished value. Ask your lender, since only CMHC Approved Lenders offer it.
grants.nextStep: Ask your mortgage lender about the CMHC Refinance for secondary suites before starting construction.

source.title: CMHC Refinance for Building Secondary Suites

grants.name: Canada Secondary Suite Loan Program
grants.amount: Was announced as up to $80,000 at 2% over 15 years (raised from $40,000 in Dec 2024). Never launched.
grants.fitNote: Cancelled. Show it only to correct older articles that still mention it.
grants.nextStep: Not available. Consider the CMHC-insured refinance instead.

source.title: Budget 2025, Annex 3: Comprehensive expenditure review (page modified 2025-11-04)
source.section: Housing, Infrastructure and Communities > Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation

process.title: Pick the route
process.detail: Basement finish (still one home: basement-finish permit, flat $351, about 10 business days) or second unit (new home: ARU permit, $392 per unit plus $0.62/sq ft, about 15 business days). Only the second-unit route triggers zoning ARU rules, the two-household fire/sound/HVAC rules and rental licensing.

source.title: Interior renovations and basements (City of Waterloo)
source.section: 6. Check permit fees; 8. Wait for review

process.title: Check zoning
process.detail: Use the City's ARU map to confirm zone, units allowed, parking and any floodplain/GRCA limits. Optional Letter of Compliance (typically 10 business days); Planning staff will pre-review plans (zoning@waterloo.ca).

source.title: Additional Residential Units Guide 2025 (City of Waterloo)

process.title: Confirm house age
process.detail: If the house has existed for at least 5 years, Part 11 compliance alternatives (Table 11.5.1.1.-C) can be used instead of some Part 9 rules; newer houses must meet new-construction rules.

source.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium

process.title: Line up money before building
process.detail: The City grant and the Region loan both reject projects already started, and CMHC must approve insured financing before construction. Apply first.

source.title: Apply for the ARU Grant (City of Waterloo)

process.title: Get drawings
process.detail: The City's ARU page lists who may prepare drawings: the homeowner for their own house (up to 2 units), or an architect, engineer or BCIN-qualified designer. The City's 2025 ARU guide says plans must be by an architect, engineer or BCIN designer (conflict; see notes). Drawings: site plan (lot, buildings, dimensioned parking, entrances), floor plans (existing/proposed, wall details, door/window sizes, lintels, ceiling heights, insulation, room names/areas, fixtures, smoke/CO alarm locations, ARU location, fire separation with rating, exits, key plans), structural plans, elevations, cross-section; HVAC (Part 6) design if a unit has 6+ bedrooms.

source.title: Build an ARU on the main floor or basement (City of Waterloo)
source.section: 4. Confirm who can prepare your drawings; 5. Prepare your drawings

process.notes: Conflict between the City web page (homeowner allowed) and the City ARU Guide 2025 p. 20 (architect, engineer or BCIN designer). The Building Code exempts a person designing a house they own from the designer registration requirement (Div. C 3.2.5.1.(3)(b)), which supports the web page.

process.title: Fill in forms
process.detail: Upload the Owner Declaration Form and Schedule 1 Designer Form (unless exempt); in person, also the Permit Application Form.

source.title: Build an ARU on the main floor or basement (City of Waterloo)

process.title: Apply and pay
process.detail: Apply on the City's building permit portal (https://building-permits.waterloo.ca/). Fee: $392 per unit added plus $0.62 per sq ft renovated, no HST; review starts after payment. Provincially mandated timeline for secondary dwelling units in houses: 15 business days from a complete application.

source.title: Check building permit timelines and fees (City of Waterloo)
source.section: Processing times by permit type; Group C residential fees

process.title: ESA electrical permit
process.detail: Electrical work needs a separate ESA permit and inspection, usually filed by a licensed electrical contractor.

source.title: Add a second unit to your house (Government of Ontario)

process.title: Build and book inspections
process.detail: Book the 'Mandatory Inspections' printed on the permit through the portal (earliest next business day) before work is covered; typical inspections: start of construction, footings, plumbing (underground, rough-in, final), framing, insulation, air barrier, final. Keep approved drawings on site.

source.title: Additional Residential Units Guide 2025 (City of Waterloo)

process.title: Occupancy and rental licence
process.detail: Renting the unit on a lease needs a City long-term rental licence (Class A when the owner does not live in that unit; new application $520-$675 for 1-5 bedrooms). From 2026-07-01 new applications need electrical and gas-appliance inspection forms, floor and parking plans. No separate ARU registration was found on the City's ARU pages.

source.title: Get a long-term rental licence (City of Waterloo)

process.title: Claim credits
process.detail: For a family suite for a senior or a relative with a disability, claim the MHRTC for the year the work is completed; for grant/loan programs, submit the occupancy permit, receipts and lease.

source.title: Line 45355 - Multigenerational home renovation tax credit (CRA)

registry.name: QuARTS Public Search Registry (Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing)
registry.searchable: Yes. Search by BCIN, organization name or individual name, or filter by Registration Type (e.g. Design Firms, Independent Designers), Classes of Registration (e.g. House, Small Buildings) and Principal Authority/Location; list or map view. Lists everyone with an active registration.
registry.termsNote: No registry-specific terms of use were found; the page carries Crown copyright (King's Printer for Ontario). Ontario's copyright page allows non-commercial reproduction with credit and no changes, and says material 'may only be reproduced for commercial purposes under a licence.' The bulk BCIN dataset on the Ontario Data Catalogue is marked as not available for privacy reasons. Safest approach: deep-link the user to the registry search with suggested filters, show only what the user looks up, and don't scrape or store listings.

source.title: QuARTS Public Search Registry

pros.whoNeedsOne: Designers who are not the owner generally must be registered (Div. C 3.2.4-3.2.5); an owner designing their own house is exempt (Div. C 3.2.5.1.(3)(b)). Architects and professional engineers are separate routes.

whoNeedsOneSource.title: 2024 Building Code Compendium, Division C Part 3

pros.cityNote: The City of Waterloo says it cannot recommend specific professionals (ARU Guide 2025, p. 17).

disclaimer: Screening aid only. Not legal, building-code, tax or financial advice, and not a permit decision. Costs are estimates, not quotes. Confirm with City of Waterloo Building Standards (building@waterloo.ca, 519-747-8712).
